condition: Suspected Sepsis AND Hypotension OR Lactate >= 4 mmol/L
recommended_action: Administer at least 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid fluid within the first 3 hours of resuscitation.

condition: Suspected Sepsis AND requirement for vasopressors
recommended_action: Target a mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65 mm Hg over higher MAP targets.
Rapid assessment of infectious vs. non-infectious causes of acute illness.

condition: High likelihood of sepsis OR septic shock
recommended_action: Administer antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition.

condition: Septic shock AND inadequate response to fluids
recommended_action: Use norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor.

condition: Septic shock AND inadequate MAP on norepinephrine
recommended_action: Add vasopressin instead of escalating dose of norepinephrine.
Obtain routine microbiologic cultures (including blood) before starting antimicrobial therapy if it does not substantially delay therapy.

condition: Requirement for piperacillin-tazobactam AND Creatinine Clearance < 20 mL/min
recommended_action: Reduce piperacillin-tazobactam dose to 2.25 g every 6 hours.

condition: Requirement for vancomycin AND Creatinine Clearance < 50 mL/min
recommended_action: Increase vancomycin dosing interval to every 24 to 48 hours based on trough levels.

condition: Requirement for meropenem AND Creatinine Clearance < 25 mL/min
recommended_action: Reduce meropenem dose to 500 mg every 12 hours.

condition: Suspected Sepsis AND End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) or severe oliguric AKI
recommended_action: Use cautious fluid resuscitation (e.g., 250-500 mL boluses) and reassess frequently, rather than fixed 30 mL/kg volume, to avoid pulmonary edema.
